s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic inflammatory condition of the nails and mucosa with possible autoimmune or infectious etiology
salient_findings: Painful swelling of the proximal nail folds
Dripping of blood from fingernails and toenails
Lichenoid plaques and erosions on the oral mucosa
Violaceous discoloration and longitudinal ridging of the nails
Raised liver enzyme levels and positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status
key_facts: Male patient in his 60s
Symptoms present for the last year
No history of preceding trauma or drug intake
Proximal nail folds are swollen and show violaceous discoloration
Nails show longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation
Partial to complete loss of nail plate with oozing of blood and hemorrhagic crusting
Oral mucosa shows lichenoid plaques and erosions
Raised liver enzyme levels
Positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status
Histopathology shows hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, and basal cell degeneration
Dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of lichenoid plaques on oral mucosa, histopathology showing hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, and basal cell degeneration

shortlist.label: Hepatitis C-associated porphyria cutanea tarda
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and symptoms consistent with porphyria cutanea tarda

shortlist.label: Hepatitis C-associated lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and clinical presentation of lichen planus

shortlist.label: Necrolytic acral erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of violaceous discoloration and necrolytic lesions on the proximal nail folds

shortlist.label: Mixed cryoglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and symptoms consistent with cryoglobulinemia

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including lichenoid plaques on the oral mucosa and dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis, are consistent with lichen planus. The presence of hepatitis C virus antibody positivity and raised liver enzyme levels suggests a connection between the hepatitis C infection and the lichen planus, making Hepatitis C-associated lichen planus the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms are consistent with lichen planus, the presence of hepatitis C virus antibody positivity suggests a specific association between the two conditions.

rejected.label: Hepatitis C-associated porphyria cutanea tarda
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms, such as lichenoid plaques and erosions on the oral mucosa, are not typical of porphyria cutanea tarda, which is characterized by blistering skin lesions and fragility.

rejected.label: Necrolytic acral erythema
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not match those of necrolytic acral erythema, which typically presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques on the feet and hands.

rejected.label: Mixed cryoglobulinemia
rejected.why: While mixed cryoglobulinemia can be associated with hepatitis C infection, the patient's symptoms do not match those of the condition, which typically presents with palpable purpura, arthralgias, and glomerulonephritis.
